subject: Phased launch / SLO mitigation proposal for Novatech integration
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: sara_patel@novatech.com, engineering@novatech.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Phased launch / SLO mitigation proposal for Novatech integration

Hi Sara / Novatech eng team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited about the product fit. Per our conversation on SLAs, I wanted to share a concrete phased-launch policy we think will let Novatech meet your latency SLOs during initial rollouts while still allowing safe production validation. High level: we propose a canary + A/B phased approach with automatic fallback to a pinned stable variant if telemetry crosses defined thresholds.

Key bullets:
- Canary window: 6–24 hours depending on traffic; start at 1% of user traffic, increase in steps (1% -> 5% -> 20%).
- Telemetry triggers: immediate automatic fallback if p95 latency increases by >40% over baseline OR error rate >1.0% sustained for 5 minutes.
- Automatic fallback behavior: swap traffic back to the prior pinned model/version within the serving cluster; pinned version remains locked for 24h after a fallback unless both parties agree on rollback extension.
- Partial pinning: ability to pin only the EU or US region independently.
- Observability: 1s token-level traces, per-route p50/p95/p99, and canary-specific dashboards.
- Rollout notification: we notify Novatech SREs via Slack + email on any autorevert event; follow-up RCA within 48 hours.

We can capture this as a short SLA carveout that says Redwood may run limited phased launches under these guardrails and will guarantee automatic fallback behavior and pinned-version protection as described. That carveout would be limited to initial launch and major model changes, not day-to-day rolling updates.

I've attached a draft policy and a small telemetry sample to show the metrics we'll monitor. Can you confirm the trigger thresholds you want in contract language? If Novatech wants a tighter bound (e.g., 120s auto-fallback requirement, different pinned-lock duration, or stricter error rate), we can adapt — we just need to understand the commercial tolerance so we can propose the formal SLA exception.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call to finalize wording.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
[d] +1 415-555-0123

From: Sara Patel <sara_patel@novatech.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Phased launch / SLO mitigation proposal for Novatech integration

Dylan — thanks, this is helpful. A few follow-ups from product and SRE: 

1) Timeline for automatic fallback: our legal/procurement wants contract language that guarantees an automated revert within 120 seconds of a trigger being detected (we understand detection latency matters; outline how you measure it).
2) Pinned duration: 24h sounds reasonable as a starting point but procurement is asking for a clause that allows us to request an extension to 72h in high-risk scenarios with 24h notice.
3) Can you confirm cross-region behavior? If EU experiences a degradation, we only want EU traffic affected and automatic fallback scoped to that region by default.
4) If autorevert happens more than twice in a 30-day window for the same release, we will request a service credit evaluation. Please propose acceptable SLO credit language.
5) SOC2 / evidence: please include the SOC2 reporting cadence and a pointer to the relevant audit artifacts for our security review.

Procurement would also like a one-paragraph summary we can hand to legal that they can redline. Can you and Laura draft a short contractual paragraph and share?

Thanks — if easier, we can take a quick call tomorrow.

Sara Patel
Product Lead, Integrations | Novatech

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: sara_patel@novatech.com
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Phased launch / SLO mitigation proposal for Novatech integration

Sara — looping in Marcus (runtime/product) and including a short contractual paragraph below plus attachments. Marcus: can you confirm the rollout automation notes on timing (we think 90–120s for a full cluster swap in typical conditions, documented runbook linked below).

Proposed contract paragraph (hand-off to legal):
"Redwood may perform controlled phased launches (canary + staged A/B) of model versions for Novatech. During a phased launch Redwood will: limit initial traffic to a configurable small percentage, monitor production telemetry in real time, and automatically revert traffic to the previously pinned model/version if any of the agreed triggers are met. Agreed automatic fallback triggers: (a) p95 latency exceeds baseline by more than 40% for a sustained period of 5 minutes, or (b) request error rate exceeds 1.0% for 5 consecutive minutes. The automatic fallback operation will be executed end-to-end within 120 seconds of trigger confirmation under normal operating conditions, and the prior model/version will remain pinned for a minimum of 24 hours following any fallback. Novatech may request an extension of the pin period up to 72 hours in exceptional circumstances with 24-hour notice. If three or more automatic fallbacks occur for the same release within a 30-day window, the parties will engage the service credit remediation process outlined in Section X."

Notes and clarifications:
- Regional scoping: automatic fallback is regional by default; cross-region swaps only occur when customers explicitly enable global rollouts.
- Telemetry and detection: detection includes streaming p95 computation and a short aggregation window; we include tracer headers for root-cause tooling.
- RCA / postmortem: we commit to a preliminary incident summary within 4 hours and a detailed RCA within 48 hours of any autorevert.
- Credit wording: propose a tiered credit of 2% monthly credit for one autorevert that results in sustained SLO breach > 1 hour, 5% credit for > 4 hours, escalating thereafter — open to negotiation.

Attachments: Novatech_phased-launch-guardrails_v1.pdf (policy draft), canary_telemetry-sample.csv (example metrics).

Related runbook: https://drive.redwood.internal/docs/Novatech-Phased-Launch-Runbook (contains exact timing expectations and rollback steps).

Marcus: confirm the 120s cluster swap SLA and whether we should propose a 90s target in preferred-customer terms.

Thanks — happy to refine.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Product — Inference Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Sara Patel <sara_patel@novatech.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 17:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Phased launch / SLO mitigation proposal for Novatech integration

Laura / Dylan — this looks good and addresses most of our asks. Procurement wants the contract paragraph as a short standalone attachment for legal redline; can you export a one-paragraph clause we can attach? Also please point to SOC2 report artifacts (or share the SOC2 attestation).

Assuming those two items, I'll route to legal and procurement today. We may ask to tighten the credit tiers but this is a good starting point.

I'll set up a short call if legal has questions.

Thanks,
Sara
